summary.text: The original bug was reproduced and the fix now passes the guard with no regressions found, but Break My Fix found an input that still breaks it: ordinal(111) returns '111st' instead of '111th'. Look next at how the fix handles the teens exception for numbers above 100 (for example 111, 112, 113), likely by checking n % 100 rather than n itself.

survivors.description: Applies the teen exception only to n%1000, so 111, 112, 113 etc. get wrong suffixes.
survivors.diff:
--- a/src/standings/ordinal.py
+++ b/src/standings/ordinal.py
@@ -16,3 +16,3 @@
         raise ValueError(f"not a position: {n!r}")
-    if n in (11, 12, 13):
+    if n % 1000 in (11, 12, 13):
         return f"{n}th"
survivors.words: src/standings/ordinal.py:17: changing `    if n in (11, 12, 13):` to `    if n % 1000 in (11, 12, 13):` made no test fail; no input tried behaved differently from the fix (it may be equivalent)
